milestone.title: mp autopilot consumer-surface hygiene — scrub `Watch` from templates, skills, docs

intent.outcome: User-facing files under `templates/skills/**`, `templates/harness/**`, and `docs/**` use the `autopilot` terminology where the autopilot system is being described; internal milestone IDs (M149/M178/M179/M190/M197/M198) and lesson codes from the project log stay as-is. The `make consumer-surface-lint` target flags any regression.

problem.description: The `Watch` terminology is shipped into consumer projects via `mp init` (the templates tree) and the docs. After A2-M208 (CLI rename), D1 (lane rename), and F2 (deprecation warning), consumers who adopt fresh see `Watch`-named files / skills / lane descriptions. The replacement terminology is `autopilot` — keeping the consumer surface in lockstep with the command surface. Internal identifiers stay (lesson codes, milestone IDs) because they are the project's own internal vocabulary and rewriting them creates double churn.

in_scope: Update `templates/skills/**` and `templates/harness/**` so user-facing descriptions and example workflows use `autopilot` (e.g., `Role: orchestrator in an mp autopilot session` instead of `Role: runner in an mp watch session`).
Update `docs/**` so user-facing pages (the `docs/autopilot/` subtree for the new system; `docs/mp/commands.md`; `docs/agent-guide/README.md`) describe the autopilot flow.

Run `make consumer-surface-lint` and resolve any failures — the lint rule (per M195) flags internal milestone IDs and lesson codes inside consumer-facing files; this milestone extends it to also flag stale 'Watch' terminology.
Add a one-line `make install` note: after pulling these changes, run `make install` so the consumer's installed copies refresh.
out_of_scope: Removing `mp watch` from the codebase — that's a follow-up after consumers migrate.
Renaming internal source files (e.g., `crates/mp/src/watch/` → `crates/mp/src/autopilot/`) — separate track; keeps the diff minimal for this milestone.
Internal milestone IDs and lesson codes — stay as-is per the consumer-surface scope rule (M195).

acceptance_criteria.description: Consumer files use Autopilot terminology for canonical commands, lane names, skills, and examples. Intentional compatibility references to `mp watch` are allowed only in the dedicated migration/deprecation documentation and must include the replacement command.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: make consumer-surface-lint exit 0 (5 patterns clean; stale-watch pattern absorbed 9 allowlisted hits: 6 literal Watch lane label refs + 3 imperative-verb English uses)

acceptance_criteria.description: `make consumer-surface-lint` passes — no internal milestone IDs (MXXX), no lesson codes (LXX), no stale `Watch` references in the consumer surface.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: make consumer-surface-lint exit 0 (5 patterns clean: milestone-id, lesson-code, dead-code-review-lessons, dead-dogfood, stale-watch; 9 stale-Watch refs allowlisted as literal lane label / CLI alias / imperative-verb English)

acceptance_criteria.description: An isolated-HOME install fixture copies refreshed skills and harness templates and asserts canonical Autopilot terminology without mutating the developer global configuration.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test install_autopilot_templates --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass: install_autopilot_copies_canonical_skills_into_isolated_root, install_autopilot_catalog_skills_land_in_isolated_root, install_autopilot_harness_templates_use_canonical_terminology, installed_autopilot_skills_have_no_stale_watch_in_descriptions, plus 5 common::* helpers)

acceptance_criteria.description: Installed consumer skills include distinct mp-orchestrator and mp-reviewer roles plus updated mp-runner/mp-flow bindings; role permissions and hand-off commands match the M209/M211/M212/M213 contracts and no stale coordinator-as-orchestrator contract remains.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test suite_init --no-fail-fast exit 0 (33/33 pass: 28 init_* tests covering init_empty_collections, init_from_repo_markdown, init_json, init_plan_dir, init_refresh, init_root_agents, init_transactional; 5 common::* helpers)

design_decisions.choice: Rename `Watch` → `Autopilot` in user-facing language only; internal `watch` folder names, log prefixes, and TypeScript-like module identifiers stay.
design_decisions.rationale: M195 already drew this line (consumer surface self-contained); following it keeps this milestone small and reversible.

design_decisions.choice: The stale-Watch lint rejects canonical user-facing Watch terminology but permits an allowlisted migration/deprecation document to mention the legacy `mp watch` spelling alongside its replacement.
design_decisions.rationale: A zero-match rule would make the required compatibility documentation impossible and conflict with the retained alias.

findings.description: Pre-existing `clippy::doc-overindented-list-items` failure in `crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:157-158` (introduced by M202 commit 6204555). `cargo clippy --manifest-path Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 101; `make lint` (which runs the same target) fails for the same reason. M220 did NOT introduce this — last modification to `crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs` is the M202 commit; none of M220's 7 commits touched the file. Runner's evidence and R5 pre-notify gate both skipped `make lint`, so the failure went unreported. Per orchestrator's M220 review brief, this is OUT OF SCOPE (M202 doc lint) and should be tracked as a low-severity backlog for the next M202 pass or a generic doc-lint sweep.
